propers.text:
Deus, omnium largitor bonorum, qui in famula tua Bibiana cum
virginitatis flore martyrii palmam conjunxisti: mentes nostras ejus
intercessione tibi caritate conjunge; ut, amotis periculis, praemia
consequamur aeterna. Per Dominum.

provenance.locator: editorial-projection artifact physical lines 1-2; antecedent 1922 Tours Mame, editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam: Commune Sanctorum printed p. 40*, artifact PDF p. 918; read on a 360 dpi render of that page (the scan's native resolution). NOT the 1862 Pustet.
provenance.provenance_authority: Triptych editorial projection verified by page-image collation against the 1962 target edition
provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1922 Tours Mame antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: Mame prints Alleluja / alleluja with j where the 1962 prints Alleluia / alleluia with i (three occurrences); no other letter differs.; no other difference: the words, their order and the pointing are identical. Corroboration: 1862 Pustet page-image collation of 2026-08-26, Pustet printed p. [32]; Internet Archive leaf n701 (Pustet Alleluja uses j; target Alleluia uses i.), outcome collated-non-exact. The Pustet's single recorded non-exactness here is the j of Alleluja. THE MAME SHARES IT. The Mame is a French printing that uses j for consonantal i throughout its body text, so its j-forms here are systematic house orthography, not a local variant. On this point the Mame AGREES WITH THE 1862 PUSTET AGAINST THE 1962, so the human review's observation stands on two independent public-domain witnesses, and no public-domain page yet seen authorises the 1962's i-spelling of this word as an exact string..
